author: Shri Raghavendra Swami
translation: V. When the accomplishment of a desire is checked by anything, anger bursts forth. Sammoha or the wrong wish is the inclination to do what ought not to be done: it may be mistaking the unrighteous conduct of appropriating another's wealth, &c, to be perfectly righteous. Front such a wrong tendency and such unrighteous activities the memory of Laws prohibiting them becomes impaired and the very sacred rules once so clearly understood by himself may now give him a very different meaning, why, they may seem to sanction to his wrong ways. Then gradually comes the loss of judgement which allows him unrestrained to be more and more wicked things. When he is thus concentrated in evil, He must purely go to hell and suffer the consequences. The significance of this genesis of passions, especially of Likes and Dislikes is: When it is known that they lead, stop by step, to hell and other sufferings, there comes the wish to get rid of them; he first ceases to muse on the objects of senses and then gradually checks the growth of those passions and eventually destroys their root. :(62 & 63.)
